reader.requirement: At --std 85, END-RETURN must close the RETURN statement so that a RETURN written with END-RETURN is a delimited scope (imperative) statement usable as the operand of another statement's conditional phrase and followed by more statements in the same scope; a RETURN without it is a conditional statement that ends at the next phrase of its container or the separator period and is refused where an imperative statement is required, and an END-RETURN with no open RETURN is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: construct conditional-phrases-any-order-2002: at 85 NOT AT END before AT END is refused (COBOL0900), at 2023 accepted (§2023:14.9.34.3 SR4)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for END-RETURN scope itself (grammar, IsConditional and VisitStatementBlock are edition-blind); the phrase ORDER inside the scope differs (85 fixed order, 2023 either order)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb350_85 and pb351 cover END-RETURN closing a RETURN inside an inline PERFORM and delimited conditionals of other verbs; not exercised: a delimited RETURN as the operand of another statement's NOT AT END followed by more statements, RETURN closed by the period, END-RETURN after AT END only, and the refusals (undelimited RETURN as an imperative, stray END-RETURN, an undelimited conditional inside RETURN's AT END)

probes.printed: R1 AAA / IF-CONT-1 / R2 BBB / READ-CONT F01 / R3 CCC / AFTER-PERIOD / SAME-SENTENCE-4 / LOOP Y / DONE (EXPECT: MATCH)
probes.expected: statements after END-RETURN run in the enclosing scope (IF branch, READ NOT AT END, same sentence, inline PERFORM); the period closes an undelimited RETURN

probes.printed: error COBOL2796: READ NOT AT END: this RETURN statement is written without its explicit scope terminator END-RETURN, so it is a conditional statement
probes.expected: refused: the NOT AT END operand is an imperative statement (§1985 IV glossary: a conditional statement is imperative only when delimited)

probes.printed: error COBOL0306: unexpected 'END-RETURN'. END-RETURN appears without a matching RETURN statement.
error COBOL2796: RETURN AT END: this READ statement is written without its explicit scope terminator END-READ
probes.expected: refused: END-RETURN closes the RETURN, so the undelimited READ inside AT END is a conditional statement where an imperative is required

probes.printed: --std 85: error COBOL0900 ... the RETURN statement writes AT END after NOT AT END, and its COBOL-85 general format prints AT END first; --std 2023: EXIT 0
probes.expected: 85 refuses the 2023 reversed phrase order within the END-RETURN scope

citations.check: OK  §1985:XI.4.3.4 GR4  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4
OK  §1985:IV.6.4.3  (6.4.3 Scope of Statements)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: The grammar's optional END_RETURN after conditionalPhrases makes the delimited form; ConditionalStatements.IsConditional reads 'phrase written and terminator absent' off the parse, and ProcedureFormatPass refuses a conditional statement in any non-IF statementBlock. All four refusal and accept probes behave per the 1985 scope rules; r2a, r2b and r2d answer identically at 2023.

refuter.evidence: (1) r3nest.cob (refute-1985-034/r3nest-001): a delimited RETURN nested in an outer RETURN's NOT AT END, followed by a statement of the outer NOT AT END and then the outer END-RETURN. Printed INNER BBB / OUTER-CONT BBB / AFTER-OUTER / EOF-INNER-2 / OUTER-CONT-2 / AFTER-OUTER-2 / DONE. Each END-RETURN closed the nearest open RETURN, per the IV.6.4.3 scope rules. (2) r4noat.cob (r4noat-001), class c: a RETURN with END-RETURN and NOT AT END but no AT END, which is outside the 1985 format where AT END is mandatory (§1985:XI.4.3.2). Refused with COBOL1850 'the AT END phrase is required on every RETURN statement'. That message cites §2023 text, which is a message-wording matter outside this rule. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XI.4.3.4 GR4  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:XI.4.3.2  (4.3.2 General Format)  the text is in the clause'.
